topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by recapping prior practical work and outlining the day's learning objectives regarding cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor Virology, Proto-Oncogenes, and Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for testing cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and Dynamics of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional definitions, cell cycle regulatory roles, and mutational behaviors of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Consequences of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the distinctions between sequence and chromosomal instability and examine their origins in defective DNA repair, replication, and mitosis.

topics.label: Multi-Step Tumorigenesis and the Vogelstein Model
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the stepwise accumulation and temporal ordering of mutations during cancer progression using the Vogelstein model.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predisposition Syndromes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how inherited mutations in gatekeeper and caretaker genes predispose individuals to cancer and influence subsequent tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with recommended reading and a preview of upcoming material.
